title: ROI Cyber-Validator Data Validation Report
framing: This project has no historical incident data for the fictional company, so predictive accuracy cannot be measured. Following data-quality best practice (dimensions used by ISO/IEC 25012 and DAMA-DMBOK), we measure (1) how faithfully our data reproduces its official sources, (2) completeness, validity and consistency, (3) traceability of every number, (4) correctness and reproducibility of the calculation engine, and (5) how stable the recommendations are when assumptions change.

scorecard.metric: MITRE fidelity / CTID fidelity / published figures
mappings backed by official sources / model inputs from published figures
acceptance tests (Python + TS) / Python–TS parity (256 configs)

mitre_fidelity.meaning: All 28 ATT&CK techniques match official MITRE v19.2 STIX data identically in ID, name, status, and associated mitigations.

ctid_fidelity.meaning: Every row of our Microsoft 365 capability mapping subset exists identically in the official CTID Mappings Explorer dataset.

published_figures.meaning: Published loss figures reproduce cited source equations exactly from FBI IC3 2025 ($123,005) and Sophos 2026 ($1,700,200).
published_figures.evidence: FBI IC3 2025 Internet Crime Report, Sophos State of Ransomware 2026

schema_validity.meaning: All 7 data files validate against strict Pydantic schemas with no missing or unknown fields.
schema_validity.evidence: Pydantic v2 validation of all backend/data JSON files

referential_integrity.meaning: All technique IDs, tool IDs, scenario definitions, and alternative routes resolve with 100% integrity.
referential_integrity.evidence: 100/100 relational cross-checks across backend data files

completeness.meaning: Every scenario step has descriptive text, names and URLs, and every technique has full descriptions and links.
completeness.evidence: 49/49 step narrative and technique metadata completeness checks

mappings_backed_by_official_sources.meaning: 74.2% of tool-to-technique mappings are backed by official MITRE or CTID datasets; unbacked claims are explicitly labeled.

model_inputs_from_published_figures.meaning: Published figures are used where public empirical data exists; remaining inputs are labeled, editable assumptions because no public per-company source exists.

ui_source_labels.meaning: Every numeric parameter displayed in the Assumptions drawer carries an explicit source label and provenance badge.
ui_source_labels.evidence: 11/11 parameter labels verified programmatically in Assumptions model

acceptance_tests.meaning: All Part C / Section 8 baseline, ROSI, what-if, and optimizer acceptance tests pass identically in Python and TypeScript.

python_ts_parity.meaning: All 2⁸ (256) tool configurations produce bit-for-bit identical rounded ALE and step outcomes across Python and TypeScript engines.

determinism.meaning: Repeated evaluations of baseline ALE and Monte Carlo distributions (seed 42) yield identical numbers.
determinism.evidence: Double-run simulation check of point ALE and PERT range percentiles

copy_compliance.meaning: Zero banned marketing claims ('100% secure', 'guaranteed', 'hack-proof') detected in code or user-facing copy.
copy_compliance.evidence: Repository scan of user-facing strings against 11 banned phrases

one_at_a_time.meaning: Varying each of the 11 assumptions by ±50% one-at-a-time never changes the recommended portfolio or Tool X finding.

joint_perturbation.meaning: Even if every assumption is off by up to ±50%, the recommended plan and the Tool X finding do not change.

limitations: No predictive validation is possible without real incident data for the fictional company.
CTID mappings use ATT&CK v16.1 while the scenarios use v19.2 (T1684.001 has no CTID row).
Published loss figures are averages across organizations of all sizes; large enterprise breach losses skew the mean.
Tool costs and attack frequencies are sample assumptions (clearly labeled in the app and editable in the Assumptions drawer).
